items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: So I called the club, got Ed Hall on the other end of the line and told him what had happened and that I was sorry but I couldn't come to work under the circumstances.

ctx.x: After the rehearsal and I was on my way home, I bought a pint of whisky, which I decided to take with me to the club. I had dinner in a restaurant and came home to change clothes. I opened my bottle and took a good taste from it and then put it in my trumpet case. Where I was living was a good 15 minutes walk to the 8th Avenue subway and when I came out to go to the gig, it was raining cats, dogs, and little fishes. I rushed to a taxi stand not far from where I lived but there were no taxis and after waiting in a…

When I arrived there, my feet were soaking wet, my pants were wet up to my knees, despite of having a raincoat on. I also had a straw hat and water was running through it down my neck and back. It was impossible for me to go play somewhere and have to sit for hours in wet clothes and wet feet. So I called the club, got Ed Hall on the other end of the line and told him what had happened and that I was sorry but I couldn't come to work under the circumstances.

Then I returned home and decided to take a hot bath to keep from catching a cold, open my bottle of juice and enjoy myself reading my papers until I got sleepy. I took my bath, but when I opened my trumpet case to take my bottle out for a nice big swig, the bottle was empty. What a bring down that was. The cork stopper had come out and the juice had dripped out in the rain. There was not one drop in the bottle and that was one of the worst nights of my life. The liquor stores were closed so I couldn't buy another…
